notes: HVS1, HVS7, and HVS8 are also cited with prior follow-up observations, but they are included in the paper's final 14-unbound sample (T:p7-b5; I:p7-b4), so they are categorized as candidates_found. HVS3 is discussed separately as a known LMC-direction HVS (T:p6-b4) and is treated as follow_up to Edelmann et al. (T:p4-b4). HVS12's earlier BHB classification (T:p6-b2) does not remove its inclusion among the 14 unbound HVSs. The four "possible HVSs" shown only as unlabeled dots in I:p7-b4/T:p7-b5 cannot be assigned unique star identifiers and are not separately listed. S0-16 (T:p3-b1) is not a Galactic unbound candidate. The Hirsch et al. star is recorded by description because no catalog identifier is supplied (T:p4-b4).

HVS1: At T:p1-b7 the paper reports the first HVS (HVS1) with a Galactic rest-frame velocity of at least +709 ± 12 km/s and a distance of 110 kpc. The paper elsewhere uses v_rf for the line-of-sight rest-frame velocity (e.g. the Fig. 3 caption at T:p7-b5), so the velocity is retained under galactic_rest_frame_velocity with a condition noting that it is not a total 3D speed. No HVS1-specific heliocentric radial velocity, parallax, or proper motion is reported in the supplied text.

HVS4: HVS4 is not given a tabulated row in the supplied text; its galactocentric radius and rest-frame velocity are read from the labeled point in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4), so the numerical values are approximate. The plotted velocity is explicitly a minimum rest-frame velocity and is not treated here as a heliocentric radial velocity.

HVS5: HVS5 is not given a tabulated row in the supplied text; its galactocentric radius and rest-frame velocity are read from the labeled point in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4). The plotted horizontal bar is described as the span of physically possible distance if the HVSs are BHB stars, not as a formal symmetric uncertainty, so no numerical error was assigned. The y-axis value is a minimum rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, not a direct 3D total speed; it is recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity with that condition.

HVS6: HVS6 is identified only in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4); the paper provides no table of individual HVS6 values. The plotted R and v_rf values and the horizontal distance span are read approximately from that figure. The plotted v_rf is a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a heliocentric radial velocity, so it is recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity rather than radial_velocity.

HVS7: HVS7 is identified in T:p6-b0 as a 3.7 M_sun Bp star. The paper does not tabulate HVS7's equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or heliocentric radial velocity. The individual quantitative values for HVS7 are read approximately from its labeled point in I:p7-b4: R ≈ 55 kpc and v_rf ≈ 405 km/s. Because T:p7-b5 labels the plotted velocity as the "minimum rest-frame velocity" and proper motion is not used, I record it as a lower limit on the Galactic-rest-frame speed rather than as a heliocentric radial velocity.

HVS8: HVS8-specific numerical values are available only graphically in Figure 3 (I:p7-b4); the extracted R ≈ 60 kpc and v_rf ≈ 410 km/s are read from the plotted labeled point. The paper does not tabulate HVS8's equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity. The plotted v_rf is a minimum rest-frame velocity, not a directly measured full three-dimensional speed.

HVS9: HVS9 is not discussed individually in the text; its individual values appear only in the labeled point in Fig. 3 (see T:p7-b5 and I:p7-b4). No right ascension, declination, heliocentric distance, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS9. The plotted values are read approximately from the figure; v_rf is a Galactic rest-frame line-of-sight minimum rather than a measured total 3D speed, and R has a plotted horizontal possible-distance range if HVS9 is a BHB star.

HVS10: HVS10 is individually labeled only in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4; T:p7-b5). The paper provides no tabulated coordinates, parallax, proper motions, heliocentric distance, or heliocentric radial velocity for HVS10. The plotted values are visually read from Fig. 3. The plotted v_rf is a minimum Galactic rest-frame line-of-sight velocity rather than a measured 3D speed, so it is reported as a lower bound on the total Galactic rest-frame velocity. HVS10 appears as one of the solid-star unbound HVSs, but no per-star bound/unbound probability is reported.

HVS11: HVS11 is not discussed numerically in the text; it is identified only as a labeled point in Figure 3 (and appears without a label in Figure 4). The Galactocentric radius is therefore an approximate graphical reading from I:p7-b4, not an exact tabulated value. The plotted v_rf is a minimum Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity rather than the star's total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed, so no velocity quantity was retained under the supplied definitions. No coordinates, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS11.

HVS12: HVS12 is mentioned textually only at T:p6-b2 as having been previously classified as a BHB star in the Sirko et al. (2004) and Xue et al. (2008) samples; no exact coordinates, parallax, heliocentric distance, proper motion, radial velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported for it. The two retained quantities are approximate readings of the labeled HVS12 point in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4). The horizontal bar in Fig. 3 indicates the possible distance span if HVS12 is a BHB star, but no exact endpoints are tabulated. The plotted v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame/minimum velocity, not a heliocentric or barycentric radial velocity.

HVS13: HVS13 appears only in Figures 3 and 4; no tabulated astrometric or velocity values are provided for it. The plotted v_rf (~447 km/s) is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, not a heliocentric or barycentric radial velocity, so it is not recorded as radial_velocity under the rules; the paper does not report a total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed for HVS13. The value R ~ 123 kpc is read graphically from Fig. 3, where HVS13 is labeled "13".

HVS14: HVS14 is not tabulated in the text; its plotted position is used from Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4). The R and v_rf values are therefore approximate readings from the figure. The plotted v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity/minimum total speed, so it is recorded as a lower bound on galactic_rest_frame_velocity rather than as radial_velocity. The horizontal error bar for HVS14 is shown but not numerically specified in the caption or text.

HVS15: HVS15 is not discussed by name in the text; its plotted values are identified from the labeled point in Fig. 3. Fig. 3's v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity/minimum space velocity, so it is not recorded as the heliocentric/barycentric radial_velocity. The plotted values are approximate read-offs because no numerical table for HVS15 is supplied.

HVS18: HVS18 is identified by the label “18” in Fig. 3 (I:p7-b4). The paper does not tabulate numerical coordinates or velocities for individual HVSs in the supplied text; the values for HVS18 are read approximately from the plotted labeled point. The horizontal error bar in Fig. 3 is described in the caption as the span of physically possible distance if the HVSs are BHB stars, not as a conventional measurement uncertainty.

HVS3: HVS3 is identified as the "unbound star very near the LMC" and as a 9 Msun B star matching the LMC abundance; the paper does not give a single explicit sentence equating HVS3 with the Edelmann et al. (2005) star, but the repeated 9 Msun B-star/LMC description links them. The only numerical velocity tied to HVS3 is the Galactic rest-frame value "at least +548 km/s"; it is a lower limit and is described as a rest-frame/line-of-sight measure rather than a measured total 3D speed. The paper gives no RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability for HVS3. The ~1000 km/s in T:p6-b5 is the ejection speed required for an LMC origin, not an observed stellar velocity, so it is not recorded as a separate measurement.

HD 271791: HD 271791 is mentioned only once, at T:p2-b5: "The star HD 271791 is the first example of an unbound 'hyper-runaway' that was ejected from the outer disk, in the direction of Galactic rotation, when its former 55 M_⊙ binary companion exploded as a supernova (Heber et al. 2008; Przybilla et al. 2008a)." This passage is qualitative: it identifies the star as an unbound hyper-runaway and gives the mass of its former companion (55 M_⊙), but reports no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactic radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for the star itself. No numeric quantity meeting the extraction rules is thus available for HD 271791.

Hirsch et al. (2005) helium-rich subluminous O star: The target star is identified only as the Hirsch et al. (2005) helium-rich subluminous O star in T:p4-b4. The paper reports only a lower limit on its Galactic rest-frame velocity and gives no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability for this star. Because the quantity is explicitly a Galactic rest-frame velocity rather than a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, it is recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity; the paper does not clarify whether the reported value is line-of-sight or total three-dimensional speed.
